reason: While this passage depicts divine judgment on Israel for covenant-breaking (destroying altars, killing prophets), it does not demonstrate antagonism toward the Hebrew people as a whole. Instead, Yahweh exhibits: (1) personal care for His faithful servant Elijah, sending angels to sustain him with food and water; (2) direct communication and purpose-giving (anointing new kings and prophets); (3) preservation of a faithful remnant of 7,000 Israelites who have not bowed to Baal. The judgment described is responsive to the people's unfaithfulness, not antagonistic in nature. Antagonism would imply fundamental opposition; instead, the text shows differentiated treatment—judgment on the covenant-breakers while maintaining relationship and preserving the faithful.
